what: A spaced repetition scheduler decides when each item should come back for review: just before you would forget it. FSRS is the modern open algorithm - it models each item's difficulty, stability and current recall probability, and sets the next review for a target recall.
like: Like watering plants that each dry out at their own pace: you water each one just before it wilts, not all of them every day.
why: Long-term memory needs review, but reviewing everything daily wastes time
Each item gets its own schedule, based on how the learner actually answered
Due reviews give the Coach agent a real reason to nudge

steps.t: Turn an answer into a rating
steps.d: Each review ends in one of four ratings: Again, Hard, Good or Easy. In a tutor, the Assessor's rubric score maps to the rating.
FSRS updates difficulty (1 to 10) and stability - the interval at which recall probability falls to 90%.
Solve the forgetting curve for the moment recall drops to your desired retention, and store that due date on the card.
A daily job gathers due cards per learner into a short review set.
The Coach agent turns due items into a nudge and a 5-minute session; answers feed back into FSRS.

choices.d: SM-2 is simple fixed multipliers; FSRS learns from review history and needs fewer reviews for the same retention.
Higher retention means more reviews; pick it per goal (exam next week vs lifelong skill).
One small, testable fact or skill per card; big topics never get a clean rating.

Delivers the nudge; FSRS decides when it's worth sending

breaks.d: A learner skips a week and 300 items are due.
breaks.see: Huge due counts, learners give up
breaks.fix: Cap daily reviews, prioritise lowest recall, spread the backlog

breaks.d: Every answer graded Good by a lenient judge.
breaks.see: Intervals grow but quiz scores fall
breaks.fix: Consistent rubric grading; calibrate the rating map

say: Every skill becomes review cards scheduled by FSRS: the Assessor's score maps to Again, Hard, Good or Easy, and FSRS sets the next due date for our target retention.
A daily job collects due cards and the Coach agent turns them into a short nudge session - that's the event trigger that brings learners back.

followups.a: Easy items waste time and hard ones are forgotten between weeks; per-item scheduling spends review time where forgetting is happening.

today: FSRS is the default scheduler in Anki and has open implementations such as ts-fsrs for TypeScript.

check.a: The interval at which recall probability falls to 90%
check.why: Stability is defined by R = 90% at t = S.

check.q: A learner returns after a week with 300 due items. Best move?
check.a: Cap today's reviews and do the lowest-recall items first
check.why: Spreading the backlog keeps learners engaged.
